To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
self supervised learning from synchronization can be used to obtain general and effective audio visual representations.

(1) a curriculum based learning scheme, (2) a contrastive loss, and (3) the use of carefully crafted negative samples are critical to obtain general and effective audio and video representations from self supervised synchronization.

(1) the visual and audial modalities are highly correlated, (2) this correlation can be used to train effective models for both modalities in a self supervised manner, (3) this can be done by optimizing a contrastive loss that measures the similarity between audio and video features, and (4) the resulting models can be further used to improve the performance on a variety of tasks.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following question: can we learn effective models for audio and visual analysis by optimizing a self supervised task? We answer positively to this question and provide evidence that our approach can yield models that are competitive to those learned from supervised training.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is able to learn general and powerful models for audio classification and video action recognition from scratch, and without any further finetuning.
our self supervised learning scheme provides an effective way to learn general audio and video representations, which are competitive with the state of the arts on established benchmarks.

our self-supervised approach can learn effective audio and visual models from scratch, without any supervision, and that these representations can be further improved by finetuning on small amounts of data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new self supervised learning framework for audio video synchronization and show that this approach is very effective for both audio classification and action recognition.

our approach is a simple and effective method for learning general audio and video models from scratch, and that our audio and visual models can be effectively used as initialization for downstream tasks.
we show how to leverage the natural correlation between the audio and video modalities to learn effective models for both.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self supervision can be an effective way to learn general and powerful models for audio and visual tasks.
the temporal correlation between audio and video is a strong signal for learning multi sensory representations, even when no supervision is available.
self supervised synchronization of audio video signals is an effective way to learn powerful representations for both modalities, which are useful in their own right.
